author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader sees every specialty with the veterinarians holding it
summary: A read-only specialty directory page lists every specialty the clinic stores, under its stored name, with each holding veterinarian named first name then last name. All specialties appear on one page. A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on it.
acceptance_criteria: every stored specialty is listed under its stored name
each specialty names the veterinarians holding it as first name then last name, for example 'Helen Leary'
a specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian named beneath it
a veterinarian holding no specialty is named nowhere on the page
every specialty appears on the one page, with no paging offered
a veterinarian holding more than one specialty is named beneath each specialty they hold (edge case 1)
the specialties are listed in a stable order, and so are the veterinarians beneath each specialty (edge case 2)
specialty names render as stored data in any chosen language, while the page's own labels are wording present in every supported language (edge case 3)
the page offers no action to create, change, or remove a specialty or a veterinarian
non_goals: managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2, confirmed unchanged by the product owner)
searching or filtering the specialty directory (NG-9)
changing the veterinarian directory REQ-VET-001, which keeps its own paging
notes: Product owner fixes the page's address at GET /specialties.html; the PRD omits addresses by house style, so the constraint is carried here. Reachability is deliberately open: whether the navigation or the veterinarian directory links to the page is an unanswered question in the PRD (raised 2026-08-04) and this slice does not depend on it. Stable order is required but the ordering key is not specified - design chooses, mirroring REQ-VET-001 edge case 1.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory stays inside the existing vet feature package (ADR 2026-07-31 feature-package-organization) and adds no module, no layer, and no dependency. It is new ground on one count: neither of the two rules that make it a specialty listing rather than a veterinarian listing can be answered from the current reads. A specialty no veterinarian holds is unreachable from Vet, and Specialty owns no reference back to Vet, so the pairing exists nowhere today. Two contracts are therefore added to the vet package and to system-design.md Contracts: SpecialtyRepository, mirroring VetRepository's plain Spring Data Repository shape in the same package, and SpecialtyDirectory, an immutable read model that pairs a whole read of specialties with a whole read of veterinarians. VetController gains the GET /specialties.html route the product owner fixed, keeping the codebase's one-controller-per-feature-package shape (OwnerController already carries six routes). ADR 2026-08-04-specialty-directory-read-model records why the pairing is assembled in a read model rather than by adding an inverse association to Specialty, and why the order is imposed in Java rather than by the query. Ordering decision: specialties by name ascending, veterinarians beneath each by last name then first name ascending, entity id as final tiebreaker. Mechanism decision: two independent read-only repository reads, no write path, NG-2 untouched.
integration_points: VetController gains GET /specialties.html returning view name vets/specialtyList; the two existing routes are untouched
VetController gains a second constructor dependency, SpecialtyRepository, alongside VetRepository
SpecialtyDirectory is built from Collection<Specialty> and Collection<Vet> by a pure static factory, so it is constructible in a unit test with no Spring context and no database
the new template renders through fragments/layout.html, which takes a menu key as its second argument
the vets cache declared in CacheConfiguration covers VetRepository reads only; the specialty read is uncached

patterns.description: repository shape to mirror for SpecialtyRepository — a plain Spring Data Repository<T, Integer> in the feature package, read methods only. Prefer this over the JPQL ORDER BY style of owner/PetTypeRepository.java:36: ordering belongs in the read model, not the query, so the page is identical on H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL whose collations differ
the existing name-ordered specialty accessor — the same Comparator.comparing(NamedEntity::getName) ordering the directory extends to the specialty list itself
the th:each table shape and the escaped ${...} rendering of stored names to follow; drop the pagination block entirely (lines 26-54) — the requirement offers no paging
the @WebMvcTest(VetController.class) + @MockitoBean repository harness the route test extends; add a @MockitoBean SpecialtyRepository beside the existing one

risks.risk: New wording in the template must exist in messages.properties and in all nine translated bundles, or I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails the build on two counts (hard-coded literal, and missing key per locale)
risks.mitigation: Add no new message key. The existing keys carry every label the page needs: #{specialties} for the heading, #{vets} for the veterinarian column, #{name} for a name column. A specialty no veterinarian holds needs no text at all — the acceptance criterion asks only that no veterinarian be named beneath it. Every literal in the template sits inside th:text

risks.risk: Passing menu key 'vets' to fragments/layout.html would highlight the Veterinarians nav item, quietly answering the PRD's open question about how a reader reaches the page
risks.mitigation: Pass a menu key matching no existing menuItem (for example 'specialties'). Nothing highlights, the nav is not edited, and the open question stays open. Do not add a nav entry or a link from vetList.html in this slice

risks.risk: An unheld specialty is not in the seed data — all three seeded specialties are held (db/h2/data.sql:12-16) — so that rule is invisible to any test reading seed data
risks.mitigation: Cover it in SpecialtyDirectoryTests with real Specialty and Vet instances constructed in the test, as VetControllerTests already constructs its vets. The five logic rules belong there, not behind MockMvc

risks.risk: Reading every veterinarian and every specialty per request is unbounded by the roster size
risks.mitigation: Accepted and recorded in the ADR's Consequences. The requirement forbids paging, the veterinarian route already reads the whole collection on its serialized route, and the vets cache absorbs the veterinarian side

risks.risk: Adding the grouping logic to VetController would be a fresh violation of the pattern catalog's Web controller row, which architecture-principles.md:91 states the existing controller deviation does not extend to
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory holds the rules; the controller reads both repositories, delegates to the factory, puts one model attribute, and returns the view name

notes: Ubiquitous language: 'Specialty directory' is already a defined term (docs/ubiquitous-language.md), which is why the read model carries that name; prose says Veterinarian, code says Vet. Name the model attribute after the domain term rather than after the collection — listVets in vetList.html is the shape to not copy. Security: the page is a parameterless read-only GET crossing no new trust boundary; stored specialty and veterinarian names are the only untrusted data rendered, and Thymeleaf's default escaping covers them, so use ${...} and never th:utext. An empty specialty table renders an empty page rather than an error, which is the fail-closed reading. The template carries no form, no POST, and no link to a mutation, so NG-2 holds by construction. Durable memory written this dispatch: docs/adr/2026-08-04-specialty-directory-read-model.md (new, indexed in docs/adr/README.md) and docs/system-design.md (two new Contracts rows, three rows amended for REQ-VET-003, one new paragraph under 'Invariants the rows cannot carry'). The prd-entry's file_targets named messages.properties; design supersedes that — the no-new-key mitigation above leaves the bundles untouched, and SpecialtyDirectory plus SpecialtyRepository are added to the target set. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op. The IDE oracle is not connected in this run; the covering-code claims above are grep-based and cite file:line, which is the weaker basis.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: SpecialtyDirectory is a well-documented immutable read model: private constructor, static factory, unmodifiable lists (verified by SpecialtyDirectoryTests' structural-change-rejection test), single responsibility per method (holdersBySpecialtyId, holdersOf, of)

Pairing by specialty id rather than object identity is correctly justified in a doc comment given the two independent read-only transactions return distinct object graphs and BaseEntity overrides no equals

The Comparator<Specialty,String>/<Vet,String> type witnesses are a necessary, narrowly-scoped workaround for a real javac inference limitation with NamedEntity::getName/Person::getLastName method references, and Comparator.nullsLast(naturalOrder()) correctly guards the nullable Integer id; both are explained in adjacent Javadoc

SpecialtyRepository mirrors VetRepository's shape (plain Spring Data Repository<T,Integer>, @Transactional(readOnly = true), Javadoc style) - confirmed by reading both files side by side; no IDE symbol-resolution oracle was available this session so this consistency check rests on a file read/grep, the weaker basis per the code-quality-review skill

VetController's new route stays a thin delegate (read both repositories, call the static factory, add one model attribute, return the view name), keeping controller logic out per the pattern catalog's Web controller row cited in the design-block and ADR

specialtyList.html's space-separated th:each span for multiple veterinarians under one specialty mirrors the existing pattern in vetList.html:20 for multiple specialties under one vet - consistent with the established template convention, not a new defect

SpecialtyDirectoryTests uses real Specialty/Vet instances (no mocks), BDD-style test names matching the PRD's acceptance criteria and edge cases, factory methods for object construction, and chained AssertJ assertions
./gradlew checkFormat passed clean on the changed files

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: No new attack surface from input: GET /specialties.html takes no path variable, query parameter, or request body, so the new route carries no user-controlled input into the application at all; the view name returned is the hardcoded literal 'vets/specialtyList', so there is no user-controlled view resolution or template-injection path.

XSS: every value in src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyList.html renders through escaped th:text (specialty name, and the ${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName + ' '} concatenation); no th:utext, th:inline, th:src/th:href over model data, inline event handler, or __${...}__ preprocessing appears in the new template. A repo-wide sweep of src/main/resources/templates/ for th:utext returns nothing, so the class has no other instance. Thymeleaf's default escaping is not disabled, matching the system-design threat-model row for rendered user data.

SQL injection: SpecialtyRepository exposes only the Spring Data derived findAll() with @Transactional(readOnly = true); no JPQL, no native query, no string concatenation. Data access stays inside the pattern the threat model records as the SQL-injection mitigation.

Data exposure: the page discloses specialty names and veterinarian first/last names, exactly the data already published unauthenticated by /vets.html and /vets. It adds no PII class, no identifier, and no operational detail. The absence of authentication and CSRF configuration is the pre-existing project-wide posture recorded in system-design.md Security Context, not a regression introduced here; the route is read-only GET with no state change, so CSRF is not applicable to it.

Secrets: a case-insensitive sweep of the full change set for token, password, secret, passwd, credential, api key, private key, bearer, and authorization returns no additions. No configuration, property file, or profile default is touched.

Supply chain: scripts/changeset.sh --name-only lists no build.gradle, pom.xml, settings.gradle, or gradle wrapper change, and git status shows those paths clean, so the dependency set and framework versions are untouched by this change and no new CVE surface is introduced. The project configures no dependencyCheck/OWASP task, so no analyzer run applies to this diff.

No deserialization, reflection, file I/O, process execution, outbound network call, or logging of user-derived data is introduced. SpecialtyDirectory is an in-memory immutable read model over two whole reads, pairing on entity id, with unmodifiable lists returned to the view.
notes: IntelliJ MCP tools were unavailable in this session, so no semantic symbol resolution backed the review; findings rest on the diff, full-file reads of the new template and the layout fragment it replaces into, and literal-string sweeps of the change set and src/main/resources/templates/. This weakens only negative claims about call sites outside the change set, none of which carry a finding here.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Two prd.md "Done when" bullets for REQ-VET-003 are satisfied only by omission in production code (specialtyList.html carries no pagination block and no mutation form/link) and have no regression test guarding them: 'all of them appear on the one page, with no paging offered' and 'it offers no action to create, change, or remove a specialty or a veterinarian'. If a future change reintroduced a paging control or an edit/delete action, no test in this suite would fail. SpecialtyDirectoryTests covers the read-model side of 'all appear' (hasSameSizeAs) but nothing exercises the rendered page for absence of paging controls or mutation actions.
findings.fix: Add assertions to the two new VetControllerTests route tests (or one more test) asserting the rendered /specialties.html body contains no pagination markers (e.g. no currentPage/totalPages model attributes, no page= link) and no create/edit/delete affordance (no <form>, no href to a mutation route).

approved_aspects: SpecialtyDirectoryTests.java exercises the read model with real Vet/Specialty instances only, no Spring context, matching the ADR's stated goal and the brief's mocking policy (real objects first)

All nine SpecialtyDirectoryTests cases use AssertJ fluent assertions, four-phase structure with blank-line separation, BDD the{Subject}Should{Outcome} naming, and named factory methods (specialty(), vet()) rather than raw constructors, with no mystery literals

Edge case 1 (holder of several specialties) and edge case 2 (stable order for specialties and for veterinarians, including a same-name entity-id tiebreak) each have dedicated, correctly targeted tests: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldNameAVeterinarianBeneathEverySpecialtyTheyHold, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOrderVeterinariansByLastThenFirstName, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOrderNamesakesByEntityId

Both PRD 'a specialty no veterinarian holds' and 'a veterinarian holding no specialty' rules are covered at both the unit level (SpecialtyDirectoryTests) and the route level (VetControllerTests), matching the ADR's stated separation of concerns rather than duplicating logic through MockMvc

Edge case 3 (stored specialty names render as data, not translated wording) is covered by the existing project-wide I18nPropertiesSyncTest, which scans the new template and would fail on a hard-coded literal or a missing translation key; the new template introduces no message key, so no new coverage gap was created

VetControllerTests' new @MockitoBean SpecialtyRepository and MockMvc usage mirror the existing sanctioned pattern (MockMvc as the one sanctioned mock, Mockito tolerated for existing-style route tests) rather than introducing a new mocking departure
./gradlew test passed clean for both files (SpecialtyDirectoryTests, VetControllerTests), and the full gate reported in build-pass at line 10 was green

semantic_surprise.note: The diff does exactly what its description says. reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers on the dispatched roster returned approved with empty findings lists, no escalate tag and no bar_clause.
